# BiSCaL <img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="120" alt="" />

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/pingbohu43/BiSCaL/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/pingbohu43/BiSCaL/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![License: GPL (>= 3)](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-GPL%20(%3E%3D%203)-blue.svg)](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0)
<!-- badges: end -->

**BiSCaL** (Bivariate Separable Causal effects in Longitudinal studies)
estimates and tests causal treatment effects on **two ordinal or
binary responses measured repeatedly over time**. For example, HDL and LDL
cholesterol recorded at every visit of a clinical trial. Responses may be
missing intermittently and follow-up may be censored. The package implements
the methods of Hu and Yi (2026, *Statistics in Medicine*).

The treatment $A$ is conceptualized as two components: $A_1$ acting on the
first response and $A_2$ on the second. Effects at the end of follow-up are
defined through generalized odds ratios (GOR) of the two responses:

* the total treatment effect $TTE_K$ compares $(A_1, A_2) = (1, 1)$ with
  $(0, 0)$;
* the separable treatment effects $STE_{1,K}$ and $STE_{2,K}$ change only the
  component acting on one response, and satisfy
  $STE_{1,K} + STE_{2,K} = 2\,TTE_K$.

The counterfactual arms $(1, 0)$ and $(0, 1)$ are identified by a recursive
formula in the transition probabilities of the responses. `BiSCaL` estimates
these probabilities by maximum likelihood and tests whether the treatment
affects one response more than the other.

## Features

* Maximum likelihood fitting of the transition and baseline models
  (baseline-category logistic regressions), with intermittent missingness and
  right-censoring handled through the observed-data likelihood.
* Binary and ordinal responses, with any thresholds of the generalized odds
  ratio.
* Total and separable treatment effects, their absolute values and difference,
  with delta-method standard errors and Wald tests, at given covariate values
  or averaged over a covariate distribution.
* Effects over the course of follow-up, with plots.
* Counterfactual joint distributions and generalized odds ratios under any
  combination of the treatment components.
* Simulators and true values for the simulation designs of the paper.
* Checked against the original research code of the paper: for the
  simulation design with complete data, the estimates, covariance matrices,
  effects and test statistics agree to numerical precision, and the effect
  computations agree with those of the data analysis.

## Installation

Install the development version from GitHub:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("pingbohu43/BiSCaL", build_vignettes = TRUE)
```

## Example

`simtrial` is a simulated trial with two binary responses, recorded at a
baseline visit and ten follow-up visits, with missingness and censoring. Fit
the models, then estimate the effects for two covariate profiles:

```{r example}
library(BiSCaL)

fit <- biscal(cbind(y1, y2) ~ x1 + x2, data = simtrial, id = "id",
              time = "visit", treatment = "trt")
summary(fit)$coefficients$beta1      # transition model for y1

aste(fit, newdata = data.frame(x1 = c(-1, 1), x2 = c(0, 1)))
```

Effects averaged over the covariates of the trial participants, and their
evolution over follow-up:

```{r population, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 3.6}
easte(fit)$effects

plot(easte(fit, K = 1:10))
```

## Main functions

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `biscal()` | Fit the transition and baseline models by maximum likelihood |
| `aste()` | Separable and total effects, and the test comparing them, given covariate values |
| `easte()` | The same averaged over a covariate distribution |
| `gor()`, `cf_prob()` | Generalized odds ratios and counterfactual joint distributions |
| `simulate_biscal()`, `biscal_coefs()`, `biscal_truth()` | Simulation designs of the paper and their true effects |

See `vignette("BiSCaL")` for a worked analysis and `vignette("simulation")`
for the simulation studies of the paper reproduced with the package.

## Citation

If you use BiSCaL, please cite the paper (see `citation("BiSCaL")`):

> Hu, P. and Yi, G. Y. (2026). Inference about separable causal effects with
> longitudinal bivariate ordinal responses with missingness and censoring.
> *Statistics in Medicine*, 45, e70320.
> [doi:10.1002/sim.70320](https://doi.org/10.1002/sim.70320)
